task_instance: Implemented the three layers described in SKILL.md (raw sources, wiki, graph) as a minimal Python package, then ingested two related sample incident-report documents (a crash report and its follow-up fix report) via ingest_with_content(), hand-extracting entities/relations as the LLM reasoning step, wrote wiki summary and entity pages with wikilinks, ran a wiki-first search plus a graph query_with_evidence() to answer 'Why does the system crash and was it fixed?' with citations back to the source documents, and ran lint_wiki() to detect and then fix a missing entity page.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/github__awesome-copilot__mini-context-graph . Built scripts/contextgraph.py (ContextGraphSkill.ingest_with_content/query/query_with_evidence) and scripts/tools/{documents_store,graph_store,wiki_store}.py implementing chunked raw-doc storage, a deduped/provenance-tracked node+edge graph with BFS (MAX_GRAPH_DEPTH=2, MIN_CONFIDENCE=0.6, MAX_NODES=50 enforced), and a markdown wiki with index.md/log.md, write_page/read_page/list_pages/search_wiki/get_log/lint_wiki. Ran `python3 run_demo.py`: ingested doc_001 (System Crash Analysis: 3 nodes, 2 edges) and doc_002 (Crash Fix Follow-up: 1 node, 1 edge added, confidence 0.9). Wrote 6 wiki pages (2 summary, 4 entity) with cross-links via [[wikilinks]]; the memory-leak entity page was updated (not re-derived) after doc_002 to add the 'resolved by' cross-reference, demonstrating compounding knowledge. wiki_store.search_wiki('memory leak') returned matching pages before falling back to the graph. skill.query_with_evidence(...) returned a subgraph of 4 nodes/3 edges plus supporting_documents=[doc_001, doc_002] and an evidence_chain citing exact supporting_text for every node/edge, confirming provenance links tie graph facts back to source text. lint_wiki() on the first pass correctly caught a real gap (an entity 'bitmap-buffer-patch' was referenced via wikilink but its entity page had not yet been written), returned it under missing_pages/broken_wikilinks; after writing that page, a re-run of lint_wiki() returned all-empty results, confirming the lint operation works end-to-end. Verified on-disk artifacts: data/documents.json, data/graph.json, wiki/index.md, wiki/log.md, wiki/summary/*.md (2 files), wiki/entity/*.md (4 files) all exist and contain the expected content (checked via `find` and `cat`/`json.tool`). No credentials, network access, or MCP/connector tools were needed; everything ran locally with the standard library.
